title: Simulacro 16 — Data pipelines: Kinesis, MSK, Glue, EMR, Athena, Redshift Spectrum
focus: Dominio 3 — Design High-Performing Architectures (24%). Ingestion, ETL, analytics batch y streaming.

questions.scenario: Un equipo evalua Kinesis para dos casos: (a) analytics real-time con custom Lambda processing sobre streams ordenados con retention 7 dias, (b) ingestion simple de logs a S3/Redshift con transformacion via Lambda, sin gestionar shards.
questions.question: Que servicio Kinesis para CADA caso?

options.text: (a) Kinesis Data Streams (KDS, con shards, retention 24h-365d, custom consumers), (b) Kinesis Data Firehose (managed near-real-time, delivery a S3/Redshift/OpenSearch/HTTP, sin shards)
options.why: Correcto. KDS = raw streams con shards, ordenados por partition key, custom consumers via KCL/Lambda/EMR, retention configurable. Firehose = managed delivery a S3/Redshift/OpenSearch/HTTP endpoints, near-real-time (buffering 60s min), sin gestion de shards, transform opcional via Lambda.
Cercano parcial pero para caso (b) delivery managed a S3, Firehose es mas simple y economico (no shards).
Incorrecto. SQS no es stream ordenado ni retention 7 dias.
Incorrecto. Firehose no permite custom consumers con logica compleja ni retention configurable extensa.

questions.explanation: Kinesis family: (1) Data Streams (KDS): raw streams, shards, ordered per shard, retention 24h-365d, consumers via KCL/Lambda/EMR/Spark Streaming/Flink. Enhanced Fan-Out (dedicated throughput per consumer). Provisioned o On-Demand. (2) Data Firehose: managed delivery, near-real-time (buffering min 60s or 1MB-128MB), sin shards, transform via Lambda, destinations S3/Redshift/OpenSearch/HTTP/3rd party. (3) Data Analytics (renamed Managed Service for Apache Flink): stream processing SQL o Flink. (4) Video Streams: media.

questions.scenario: Una empresa tiene Kafka on-prem con ecosistema robusto (Kafka Connect, Schema Registry, ksqlDB). Quieren mover a AWS managed sin cambiar codigo cliente Kafka.
questions.question: Que servicio AWS es Kafka-compatible managed?

options.text: Amazon MSK (Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka): Kafka managed, compatible con Kafka API, ecosystem Kafka (Connect, Streams, Schema Registry)
options.why: Correcto. MSK es Kafka managed: same Kafka clients, MSK Connect (Kafka Connect managed), Schema Registry via Glue, ksqlDB via KRaft/Zookeeper managed. Ideal para migrar Kafka on-prem sin refactor.
Cercano funcional (streaming ordenado) pero API distinta (no Kafka); requiere refactor codigo cliente.
Cercano pero perdiendo el beneficio managed. MSK es la opcion managed.
Incorrecto. Firehose es managed delivery, no Kafka.

questions.explanation: MSK: Apache Kafka managed. Options: (1) MSK Provisioned (brokers gestionados). (2) MSK Serverless (pay per throughput, sin gestionar broker capacity). Componentes ecosistema: MSK Connect (Kafka Connect managed), Glue Schema Registry (schema evolution), ksqlDB self-managed. Casos: migracion Kafka on-prem, ecosistema Kafka rico. Precio: por broker hora + storage + data transfer. Kinesis vs MSK: Kinesis mas simple y AWS-native; MSK mas potente y Kafka ecosystem.

questions.scenario: Un equipo tiene datos en S3 (JSON, Parquet, CSV) y quiere hacer queries SQL ad-hoc sin ETL previo ni infrastructure de warehouse.
questions.question: Que servicio AWS permite queries SQL directly on S3?

options.text: Amazon Athena: serverless SQL query engine sobre S3 (Presto-based), sin infrastructure, pay per data scanned
options.why: Correcto. Athena es serverless SQL sobre S3 data. Sin cluster gestionar. Precio por GB scanned. Optimizable con formats columnar (Parquet, ORC) + particionamiento (por date, region). Ideal ad-hoc queries, log analytics, business analytics on S3 data lake.
Cercano pero requiere cluster (o Serverless) y COPY data al warehouse; Athena queries direct on S3.
Cercano parcial (EMR con Presto ofrece funcionalidad similar) pero requiere provisionar cluster; Athena es serverless.
Incorrecto. RDS no query direct S3 files nativamente.

questions.explanation: Athena: serverless SQL sobre S3, basado en Presto/Trino. Precio: $5/TB scanned. Optimizaciones: (1) formats columnar (Parquet, ORC) reducen scan hasta 90%. (2) Particionamiento (year/month/day) reduce scan a subset. (3) Comprension (gzip, snappy). (4) Bucketing para joins. (5) AWS Glue Data Catalog para metadata (schema on read). Athena Federated: query across data sources (RDS, DynamoDB, ElastiCache, etc.). Casos: ad-hoc analytics, log analysis, one-off business queries.

questions.scenario: Un data engineer necesita: crawler que descubra schema de S3 datasets, ETL jobs escalables en Spark, y catalog central de metadata compartible entre Athena/Redshift/EMR.
questions.question: Que servicio AWS provee esto integrado?

options.text: AWS Glue: crawlers (auto-descubrir schema), ETL jobs Spark-based (serverless), Data Catalog (metadata central Hive-compatible), Studio (visual editor), Data Quality
options.why: Correcto. Glue es la suite ETL/catalog managed. Crawlers escanean S3/JDBC y populan Data Catalog. Jobs corren Spark serverless (glue etl v3+). Studio visual DAG editor. Compartible con Athena/Redshift Spectrum/EMR/Lake Formation.
Cercano funcional (Spark on EMR) pero requiere gestionar cluster y no incluye catalog nativo (usar Glue Catalog externo).
Cercano solo para small transforms; no escala a big data batch.
Incorrecto. Data Pipeline es legacy (deprecated), Glue es el sucesor moderno.

questions.explanation: AWS Glue componentes: (1) Data Catalog: metadata central Hive Metastore-compatible, compartible cross-service. (2) Crawlers: auto-discovery de schema desde S3/JDBC. (3) Glue ETL Jobs: Spark/Python serverless, PySpark/Scala. (4) Glue Studio: visual DAG editor. (5) Glue DataBrew: no-code data prep. (6) Glue Data Quality: quality rules automation. (7) Glue Streaming ETL: streaming pipelines. Precio: por DPU-hour + Data Catalog storage/requests. Combinable con Lake Formation para governance.

questions.scenario: Un equipo big data necesita ejecutar workloads Hadoop, Spark, Presto, Hive, HBase sobre 500TB de datos con control total del cluster (Hadoop tuning avanzado).
questions.question: Que servicio AWS provee cluster managed Hadoop/Spark?

options.text: Amazon EMR (Elastic MapReduce): cluster managed Hadoop/Spark/Presto/Hive/HBase con nodes EC2 o EKS o Serverless
options.why: Correcto. EMR es managed Hadoop ecosystem. Deployment options: EC2 (control total, cluster manual scaling), EKS (containers), Serverless (pay per job). Frameworks: Spark, Hive, Presto/Trino, HBase, Flink, Ganglia. Casos: big data batch, ML training, log analytics masivos, ETL a escala.
Cercano para ETL simple pero limitado en tunning avanzado Hadoop y ecosystem breadth (HBase, Flink). EMR mas potente y control.
Incorrecto. Redshift es warehouse OLAP, no Hadoop/Spark ecosystem.
Cercano solo para SQL queries; no ejecuta Hadoop/Spark workloads generales.

questions.explanation: Amazon EMR: managed Hadoop ecosystem on AWS. Deployment: (1) EMR on EC2 (traditional, control cluster capacity, RI/Spot). (2) EMR on EKS (containers, mejor multi-tenancy). (3) EMR Serverless (pay per job, cero cluster mgmt, ideal casos variables). Frameworks: Spark, Hive, Presto/Trino, HBase, Flink, Zeppelin. Casos: big data ETL, ML training, log analytics masivos, genomics, media processing. Storage: HDFS local + S3 (EMRFS). Combinable con Glue Catalog.

questions.topic: Redshift Spectrum para data lake queries
questions.scenario: Un cliente tiene Redshift warehouse con datos hot (ultimos 90 dias) y cold data (2 anos+) en S3 Parquet. Quieren ejecutar queries que combinen ambos sin cargar cold data al warehouse.
questions.question: Que feature Redshift permite query hybrida warehouse + S3?

options.text: Redshift Spectrum: external tables sobre S3 (formats Parquet, ORC, JSON, CSV) queryable con SQL Redshift; JOINs entre warehouse tables y S3 external tables
options.why: Correcto. Spectrum extiende Redshift a S3 data lake. External tables via Glue Catalog. Queries pueden combinar internal (fast columnar warehouse) y external (S3). Ideal lakehouse pattern: hot data in warehouse, cold data in S3, query unified.
Cercano funcional pero costoso storage warehouse. Spectrum permite queryar sin cargar.
Cercano para S3 pero no une con warehouse tables Redshift en single query.
Cercano lakehouse extremo pero sacrifica perf de warehouse para hot queries.

questions.explanation: Redshift Spectrum: external tables sobre S3, queryables con SQL Redshift, JOINs cross-source. Precio: $5/TB scanned (mismo Athena base). Requires Glue Catalog o Hive Metastore. Best practices: (1) formats columnar (Parquet, ORC) para eficiencia scan, (2) particionamiento para pruning, (3) manifests para consistencia, (4) offloader design (hot to warehouse, cold to S3). Lakehouse pattern: warehouse + S3 + Spectrum, con AWS Lake Formation para governance.

questions.scenario: Una empresa multi-cuenta tiene un data lake en S3 con multiples usuarios (analistas, data scientists, apps). Necesitan governance: permisos fine-grained por columna, tag-based access, audit centralizado, data sharing entre cuentas.
questions.question: Que servicio AWS gestiona governance de data lakes?

options.text: AWS Lake Formation: governance layer sobre S3 + Glue Data Catalog con permissions granular (row, column, cell), tag-based access, cross-account sharing, audit
options.why: Correcto. Lake Formation es governance managed para data lakes AWS: fine-grained access (row/column/cell level), tag-based (LF-Tags), cross-account data sharing via Data Catalog, audit unified, integrated con Athena/Redshift/EMR/Glue.
Cercano pero IAM es coarse-grained (bucket/prefix), no column/row level. Lake Formation anade granularity.
Cercano pero limitado a permissions object-level, no columnar.
Cercano complementario. Lake Formation usa Glue Catalog debajo pero anade governance layer con LF permissions y LF-Tags.

questions.explanation: AWS Lake Formation: governance layer para data lakes S3. Features: (1) Fine-grained permissions: database/table/column/row/cell level. (2) LF-Tags (Lake Formation Tags): tag-based access control (Attribute-Based Access Control - ABAC). (3) Cross-account data sharing via Data Catalog. (4) Blueprint (workflow) para ingest. (5) Governed tables con ACID (transactions, time travel). (6) Data filters (predicate-based access). Integrated con Athena, Redshift Spectrum, EMR, Glue, QuickSight. Requires Data Catalog.

questions.scenario: Un equipo quiere procesar streams en tiempo real con SQL o Apache Flink: agregar metrics por ventanas, detectar anomalias, sesionizar events, enriquecer con lookup tables.
questions.question: Que servicio AWS provee stream processing managed?

options.text: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink (formerly Kinesis Data Analytics): stream processing con Flink SQL/Java/Scala, windowing, joins, enrichment
options.why: Correcto. Managed Flink es el servicio managed para stream processing: Flink runtime managed, integrated con Kinesis/MSK/otras sources, windowing (tumbling, sliding, session), aggregations, joins, exactly-once semantics. Renamed 2023 de Kinesis Data Analytics for Apache Flink.
Cercano simple pero limitado para windowing/stateful complex processing. Flink es purpose-built.
Cercano funcional (Spark Streaming/Structured Streaming) pero requiere gestionar cluster. Managed Flink es serverless.
Incorrecto. Athena es batch SQL, no stream processing continuo.

questions.explanation: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink: stream processing managed. Runtime Flink (also Studio Notebooks para dev interactivo). Sources: Kinesis Data Streams, MSK, Firehose. Sinks: Kinesis, Firehose, Lambda, S3, DDB. Casos: real-time metrics/dashboards, anomaly detection, sessionization, event correlation, streaming ETL. Alternativas: Lambda triggers (simple), EMR Spark Streaming (control cluster), self-managed Flink en EKS.

references.title: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink

questions.scenario: Un equipo streamea CloudWatch Logs a S3 via Firehose. Necesitan: (1) transformar cada record (parse JSON, enriquecer con lookup), (2) convertir formato de JSON a Parquet para eficiencia Athena, (3) enrutar records segun contenido a diferentes S3 prefixes.
questions.question: Que features de Firehose cubren esto?

options.text: Data Transformation via Lambda (parse/enrich), Format Conversion built-in (JSON to Parquet/ORC), Dynamic Partitioning (route por content a prefixes)
options.why: Correcto. Firehose soporta: Data Transformation (Lambda pre-delivery), Format Conversion nativo JSON<->Parquet/ORC (con Glue Catalog schema), Dynamic Partitioning (partition keys extraidas del content, ej. year=/month=/day=). Cumple los 3 requisitos declarativamente.
Cercano pero reinventa Firehose managed features. Delivery a S3 con transforms es exacto para Firehose.
Cercano pero KDS es raw stream sin managed delivery ni transforms. Firehose lo hace todo.
Cercano batch pero pierde near-real-time delivery de Firehose.

questions.explanation: Kinesis Firehose features: (1) Data Transformation: Lambda invocada antes de delivery para transform/enrich/filter. (2) Format Conversion: JSON to Parquet or ORC (necesita schema del Glue Catalog), reduce scan cost downstream Athena/Spectrum. (3) Dynamic Partitioning: extrae partition keys del payload (usar JQ syntax), rutea a prefixes distintos. (4) Buffering: por tamano (1MB-128MB) o tiempo (60s-900s). (5) Compression: gzip, snappy, zip. Destinations: S3, Redshift (via COPY), OpenSearch, HTTP, 3rd party (Datadog, Splunk).

questions.scenario: Un negocio quiere dashboards BI managed sin desplegar Tableau/Looker, conectados a Redshift/Athena/S3/RDS con controles fine-grained de acceso por rol.
questions.question: Que servicio AWS provee BI managed?

options.text: Amazon QuickSight: BI managed con SPICE (in-memory calculation engine), conectores a Redshift/Athena/S3/RDS/etc., ML insights, embedded analytics
options.why: Correcto. QuickSight es BI managed AWS-native. SPICE (Super-fast Parallel In-memory Calculation Engine) acelera dashboards. Conectores a data sources AWS + 3rd party. ML Insights (anomaly detection, forecasting). Embedded analytics para apps. Precio: per user (reader vs author) o session (embedded).
Cercano parcial para AWS metrics pero no BI para datos negocio (data sources externos, complex visualizations).
Cercano queries pero sin visualization UI.
Cercano para logs (OpenSearch Dashboards) pero orientado a logs, no BI general.

questions.explanation: Amazon QuickSight: BI managed. Editions: Standard (basic), Enterprise (SPICE 500GB por user, SSO SAML/OIDC, row-level security, VPC connectivity, ML insights). SPICE: in-memory engine que acelera queries. Data sources: AWS services (Redshift, Athena, S3, RDS, Aurora), 3rd party (Salesforce, Snowflake, Teradata, MySQL), files (CSV, XLSX). Features avanzadas: ML Insights (anomaly detection, forecasting), Embedded Analytics (dashboards en tu app), QuickSight Q (natural language queries).

questions.scenario: Un data lake almacena logs JSON. Athena queries son lentos y caros (scans multi-TB). Un consultor recomienda cambiar formato.
questions.question: Que formato optimiza queries analytics y por que?

options.text: Parquet (o ORC): formato columnar comprimido; queries que selectan pocas columnas scanean solo esas (no todo el row), reduciendo I/O 90%+
options.why: Correcto. Parquet es columnar (columnas juntas), permite: (1) column pruning (scan solo columnas del SELECT), (2) predicate pushdown (skip row groups con filtros), (3) mejor compression (columnas de mismo type comprimen mejor). Reduce coste Athena/Spectrum drasticamente. Format estandar analytics.
Incorrecto. Row-based, texto sin comprimir, scans todos los bytes.
Incorrecto. Row-based, verbose, sin column pruning eficiente.
Cercano (Avro es row-based binary con schema, ideal para streams/serializacion Kafka) pero no columnar; para analytics Parquet/ORC son superiores.

questions.explanation: S3 formats para analytics: (1) CSV/JSON: text, row-based, verbose, sin column pruning. Malo para queries. (2) Avro: binary row-based con schema, ideal streaming/serializacion. (3) Parquet: columnar, comprimido (Snappy default), column pruning, predicate pushdown. Estandar analytics (Spark, Athena, Spectrum). (4) ORC: similar a Parquet, optimizado Hive. Compression codecs: Snappy (rapido), Gzip (mejor ratio), Zstd (balance). Best practices: convertir a Parquet + particionamiento (fecha, region) + compression.

questions.scenario: Una empresa migra 50 TB de datos on-prem NFS/SMB a S3 y EFS. Necesitan transferencia acelerada, verificacion de integridad, y bandwidth throttling.
questions.question: Que servicio AWS es purpose-built para bulk data transfer?

options.text: AWS DataSync: agente on-prem transfiere a S3/EFS/FSx con encryption, integrity checks, bandwidth throttling, scheduling, incremental transfers
options.why: Correcto. DataSync es purpose-built bulk transfer: agente on-prem (VMware/Hyper-V/EC2/KVM) transfiere via network optimizado (10x faster que scp/rsync), integrity checks, bandwidth throttling, scheduling, incremental sync. Destinations: S3, EFS, FSx (Windows, Lustre, ONTAP, OpenZFS).
Cercano funcional pero mucho mas lento y sin scheduling/incremental sofisticados. DataSync es hasta 10x mas rapido.
Cercano pero Storage Gateway es hybrid ongoing (cache/gateway), no purpose-built para migration bulk one-time.
Cercano para petabytes offline (>100TB) pero 50TB puede hacerse online con DataSync mas rapido/simple.

questions.explanation: AWS transfer services: (1) DataSync: online bulk transfer (agente NFS/SMB/HDFS/self-managed object stores -> S3/EFS/FSx). Optimizations, incremental, scheduling. Casos: migration/replication ongoing. (2) Snow Family (Snowball, Snowmobile, Snowcone): offline (physical devices) para petabytes o low-bandwidth locations. (3) Storage Gateway: hybrid cache/tape/file gateway ongoing (no migration one-time). (4) Transfer Family: SFTP/FTPS/FTP protocol for user uploads. (5) S3 Transfer Acceleration: web upload acceleration via CloudFront.
